newsitem.title: GERMANY: 3,000-point level on DAX expected to hold-dealers.
newsitem.headline: 3,000-point level on DAX expected to hold-dealers.

text.p: German stock market analysts said that they expected the 3,000-point level, which was penetrated in electronic trade earlier in the day, to hold over the coming period.
The IBIS DAX-30 index closed at 3,006.87 points, up 10.75.
German shares were boosted all day by the dollar trading at 30-month record highs and an options expiry. A firm opening on the Dow Jones Industrial index boosted the market.
Some dealers remained cautious. "Only when we are 30 points above the 3,000-point mark will I really believe that we have conclusively penetrated the 3,000-point level."

Analysts at both Vereins-und-Westbank and Berenberg Bank said they thought that German shares would continue to rise in the near future and that the DAX index would remain above 3,000 points in the foreseeable future.
Deutsche Bank was a volume leader and finished the day up 35 pfennigs at 78.90 marks, while Dresdner Bank finished up 1.25 marks at 52.55 marks.
Commerzbank ended the day up 50 pfennigs at 43.90, having been boosted over the day by remarks by its chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen that he thought the share was undervalued.

Daimler-Benz AG ended the day up 2.10 marks at 117.10 marks. The market took in its stride the news on Thursday that Mercedes chief Helmut Werner was leaving the group over a disagreement on management restructuring.
"This is certainly not a negative for Daimler. Of course Werner is a great man but people will still have a high opinion of Daimler," said a Munich trader.
